Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Self-reported sadness/depression was less prevalent in vitamin D sufficient adolescents than in insufficient or deficient ones.
Sentence: "The prevalence of self-reported anger, anxiety, poor quality sleep, sadness/depression, and worry was significantly lower (P < 0.05) in vitamin D sufficient participants compared with their other counterparts."
Measured as: self-reported sadness/depression
Population: 1095 Iranian school students, mean age 14.7 years
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D status (sufficient vs insufficient vs deficient), observational
Comparator: Vitamin D insufficient and deficient groups
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 1,095
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Genetically determined higher serum 25(OH)D was not associated with depression in Mendelian randomization using UK Biobank data.
Sentence: "In MR inverse variance weighted (IVW) using the UK Biobank, there was no association between genetically determined serum 25(OH)D and depression (OR per 50% higher 0.97, 95%CI 0.90-1.05) with consistent null association across all MR approaches and in data from PGC consortium."
Measured as: depression
Population: White British UK Biobank participants (up to 307,618) plus SUNLIGHT and PGC consortia summary data
Intervention: Genetically determined serum 25(OH)D (Mendelian randomization)
Comparator: Lower genetically determined 25(OH)D
Design: other primary study
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both findings bear on vitamin D and depression, but a cross-sectional association in adolescents points the opposite way from a null Mendelian randomization result, so the disagreement is genuine and attributable to study design.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","outcome_measure"],"detail":"design: cross-sectional serum 25(OH)D status vs Mendelian randomization with genetic proxy; also adolescents (n=1,095) vs adult UK Biobank, self-reported sadness vs depression diagnosis"}
